REPLACE-WITH-ORGANIZATION.meaning: The organisation's name, as the session banner and the auto-mode environment should state it

REPLACE-WITH-PRIMARY-USE.meaning: One phrase for what the fleet is used for - the auto-mode classifier reads it to judge what is in scope

REPLACE-WITH-CLOUD-PROVIDERS.meaning: The cloud providers your work legitimately talks to, or none

REPLACE-WITH-STORAGE-DESCRIPTION.meaning: One phrase for where project data lives (for example: shared network filesystems under a project root)
REPLACE-WITH-STORAGE-DESCRIPTION.example: shared network filesystems under a project root

REPLACE-WITH-INTERNAL-DOMAIN.meaning: Your internal DNS domain - hosts under it are treated as inside the organisation

REPLACE-WITH-SITE-NAME.meaning: A short name for this deployment, used where the tooling labels its own output

REPLACE-WITH-SUPPORT-EMAIL.meaning: The address a blocked engineer is told to write to

REPLACE-WITH-BANNER-ART.meaning: The banner shown at session start - plain text, or your own art

REPLACE-WITH-SENSITIVE-DATA-LOCATIONS.meaning: Where the site's sensitive data lives and who may see it, as one phrase. The auto-mode classifier reads it to judge whether an action exposes that data
REPLACE-WITH-SENSITIVE-DATA-LOCATIONS.example: customer deliverables under /projects, shared only within the assigned project team

REPLACE-WITH-HOST-DESCRIPTION.meaning: One phrase describing the host and the data it holds, beginning with an article. The auto-mode classifier reads it as context for every decision
REPLACE-WITH-HOST-DESCRIPTION.example: a shared multi-user Linux workstation holding customer data under NDA
